_source: Mongoose Traveller 2e Core Rulebook Update 2022, printed pp47 and 50 (pdf 40 and 43)

other_benefits._intro: Granted when you leave a career in good standing. Different careers grant different Benefits. Nearly every entry has a DUPLICATE rule -- what happens if you roll the same Benefit again -- so benefits are NOT idempotent and the engine must track how many times each has been taken.

Armour.grant: any type of armour, limit Cr10000 and TL12
Armour.duplicate: select another type within the same limits, or trade the original in for armour with a limit of Cr25000

Blade.grant: any blade weapon, limit Cr1000 and TL12
Blade.duplicate: another blade, or one level in Melee (blade)

Characteristic Increase.grant: increase the listed characteristic by the amount shown, up to your racial maximum (15 for humans)
Characteristic Increase.overflow: increases above 15 are LOST -- EXCEPT SOC: every point of excess SOC becomes a Ship Share
Characteristic Increase._note: The SOC overflow rule is the one characteristic-cap exception in creation. Do not clamp SOC silently.

Cybernetic Implant.grant: any augmentation, limit Cr75000 and TL12
Cybernetic Implant.duplicate: take a different augmentation, or increase one you already possess by one level of Improvement (this may exceed the Credit and TL limit)

Free Trader.grant: a free trader with 25% of the mortgage paid off; roll 1D times on the Spacecraft Quirks table
Free Trader.duplicate: a further 25% of the mortgage paid off; four times clears it entirely
Free Trader.alternative: may select a far trader instead

Gun.grant: any common or military ranged weapon, limit Cr3000 and TL12
Gun.duplicate: another weapon, or one level in the appropriate Gun Combat skill for a weapon already received as a Benefit

Lab Ship.grant: a lab ship with 25% of the mortgage paid off; roll 1D times on the Spacecraft Quirks table
Lab Ship.duplicate: a further 25% of the mortgage paid off; four times clears it entirely

Personal Vehicle.grant: a personal vehicle such as a ground car or air/raft, limit Cr300000 and TL10; may not be armed
Personal Vehicle.duplicate: gain a level of Drive or Flyer

Scientific Equipment.grant: any one piece of scientific equipment, limit Cr2000 and TL12
Scientific Equipment.duplicate: another piece, or one level in Electronics or Science

Scout Ship.grant: a scout ship; you have full use of it and may modify it, but it still belongs to the Scout Service and can be recalled, so you will be expected to run missions from time to time

Ship's Boat.grant: a ship's boat or other small craft, limit MCr10 and TL12

Ship Shares.grant: one or more Ship Shares toward obtaining a ship; each is worth MCr1 and cannot be redeemed for cash

Weapon.grant: any weapon, limit Cr3000 and TL12
Weapon.duplicate: another weapon, or one level in the appropriate Melee or Gun Combat skill for a weapon already received as a Benefit

TAS Membership.grant: membership of the Travellers' Aid Society: hostels and facilities at all Class A and B starports, available at reasonable cost to members and guests
TAS Membership.duplicate: see mustering-out.json -- rolling it again yields two Ship Shares
TAS Membership.purchasable: membership may also be bought for MCr1, though an application can be black-balled by an existing member

skill_packages._rule: As a group, all Travellers select ONE package between them. Each Traveller then takes turns selecting an item from the package until all skills have been taken.
skill_packages._single_character_note: This is a group rule. For a one-Traveller generator, present the package and let the user take the skills they would plausibly have claimed, or offer the whole package as a reference. Do not silently grant all of it.

Traveller.desc: An all-round package, good for a campaign where the Travellers are trading one week and blowing things up the next.

Trader.desc: For campaigns where trading and commerce are the primary activities.

Explorer.desc: For campaigns on the fringe of Charted Space, dealing with new worlds and ancient relics.

Investigator.desc: For campaigns centring on solving crimes and investigating mysteries.

Mercenary.desc: Focused on ground combat, aimed at combat-heavy games.

Starship.desc: For campaigns where the Travellers spend almost all their time on spacecraft.

Diplomat.desc: For campaigns where the Travellers are government operatives and ambassadors.

Criminal.desc: For campaigns involving crime and elaborate heists.

_mercenary_note: The Mercenary package genuinely lists Gun Combat 1 twice, as printed. Most packages hold 8 skills; Investigator holds 9.
